items.title: VLANs on the board's switch, with apply-then-confirm
items.summary: **VLANs on the board's switch — shipped in firmware v2.33.0, with three ways to use them**

items.title: A hardware watchdog, so a hung daemon does not mean a trip to the rack
items.summary: The SoC has a watchdog and this firmware does not arm it.

items.title: Remote syslog, and an audit line for every mutating API call
items.summary: Ship the board's logs somewhere that survives it, and write one line per call that changes state — who, what, from where.

items.title: Manage the BMC's SSH keys and change its password from the interface and the fleet
items.summary: The only way to put an SSH key on the BMC, or take one off, is to log in over SSH and edit `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` by hand.

items.title: OpenTelemetry: traces, logs and metrics over OTLP, opt-in
items.summary: The board already exposes Prometheus metrics on their own credential-free listener, which is the right thing when the cluster is down.

items.title: SD card: checksums computed on the board, upload, rename and move
items.status: Listing shipped in v3.25.0; the rest is open
items.summary: The interface can now list what is on the card and say which files can be written to a module (v3.25.0).

items.title: Choose the self-signed certificate's key type and validity
items.summary: When no operator certificate is installed the board issues its own: EC P-384, real names, 825 days, renewed 30 days out.

items.title: Install a certificate from your own CA
items.summary: If you run a private certificate authority — step-ca, your router's, your own — you can already trust its root in your browser and get a green padlock on anything it issues.

items.title: ACME against a private CA, so the certificate renews itself
items.summary: ACME is a protocol, not a company.
